name: RustDesk
description:
Your own RustDesk server: the ID server and the relay, with a web console, user accounts, an address book that follows you to every client and a web client in the browser. Devices can also change their ID, which the stock open-source server refuses.

What you get:
• Web console at /_admin/ on port 21114: devices, users, groups, address books, connection and file transfer logs
• Log in once in the RustDesk client and your address book is on every device
• Web client at /webclient/ for a session from any browser
• "Change ID" in the client works, for the machine that registered the old ID and a free new ID
• Encrypted connections only, by default

Notes:
• Fill in the four address fields with the name or IP your clients reach this server under.
• The first start creates the key pair in the data folder and prints the console's admin password in the container log (search for "Admin Password").
• Moving from another RustDesk server: copy id_ed25519, id_ed25519.pub and db_v2.sqlite3 into the data folder before the first start, and every device keeps its ID.
• Clients need the ID server (port 21116), the relay (21117), the API server (http://...:21114) and the key from id_ed25519.pub.

Source on GitHub: https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/rustdesk

paths.name: Server data (/data)
paths.description: Key pair (id_ed25519, id_ed25519.pub) and the device database. Keep it: a new key pair means every client has to be set up again.

paths.name: Console data (/app/data)
paths.description: Users, groups, address books and logs of the web console.

ports.name: Console and web client
ports.description: Web console (/_admin/), the API the clients log in to, and the web client (/webclient/). Only needed inside your network unless you want to log in from outside.

ports.name: NAT test
ports.description: Lets clients find out what kind of NAT they are behind.

ports.name: ID server (TCP)
ports.description: ID server and hole punching. Forward it if devices outside your network connect.

ports.name: ID server (UDP)
ports.description: ID server registration and hole punching over UDP.

ports.name: Relay
ports.description: Relay for sessions whose devices cannot reach each other directly.

ports.name: ID server (websocket)
ports.description: ID server over websocket, used by the web client.

ports.name: Relay (websocket)
ports.description: Relay over websocket, used by the web client.

variables.name: Relay address (RELAY)
variables.description: Name or IP and port of the relay as clients reach it, e.g. rustdesk.example.com:21117.

variables.name: ID server for clients
variables.description: The ID server address the console hands to clients, e.g. rustdesk.example.com:21116.

variables.name: Relay for clients
variables.description: The relay address the console hands to clients, e.g. rustdesk.example.com:21117.

variables.name: API server for clients
variables.description: The console's address as clients reach it, e.g. http://rustdesk.example.com:21114.

variables.name: Encrypted connections only (ENCRYPTED_ONLY)
variables.description: 1 accepts only clients that know the server's key. 0 also lets clients without the key connect.

variables.name: Login required (MUST_LOGIN)
variables.description: Y lets only clients that are logged in to the console start a session.
